subject.title: [Feature]: Telegram quote/reply context should be a first-class, durable inbound contract instead of a split prompt/runtime patch surface

question: Should this issue remain the umbrella for both the documented inbound reply-metadata contract and the newly reported Telegram outbound selected-text Quote UX, or should the outbound behavior be split into a separate scoped report while the linked runtime PR and fixture complete the inbound work?
rationale: The supplied discussion supports a concrete inbound contract and an open implementation candidate, but the latest outbound report proposes a potentially different Telegram delivery tradeoff that needs an explicit ownership and product-scope decision.

options.title: Split outbound Quote UX
options.body: Keep this issue focused on structured inbound reply metadata and regression coverage, and create or revive a separate scoped tracker for outbound Telegram selected-text Quote compatibility.

options.title: Keep one umbrella issue
options.body: Retain both paths here, but require separate acceptance criteria and ownership for inbound runtime context versus outbound delivery behavior.

recommendation.title: Split outbound Quote UX
recommendation.body: Keep this issue focused on structured inbound reply metadata and regression coverage, and create or revive a separate scoped tracker for outbound Telegram selected-text Quote compatibility.

likelyOwner.reason: The open linked PR is the clearest current implementation path for the inbound runtime contract, making its author the best available routing candidate for the scope discussion.
